item.text: The basic CLI and output path is matching. I’m running a broader regression sweep now: a batch compare over irregular nouns plus the parser edge cases that `argparse` handled in a non-obvious order.

The first broad compare was blocked by command-safety rules because I used temp-file cleanup. I’m rerunning the same verification with pure shell capture so I can finish the comparison without touching files.

item.command:
/bin/bash -c "set -e
cases=(
  \"--a x,y --b item\"
  \"--a a,b,c --b wish\"
  \"--a a,b --b box\"
  \"--a a,b --b baby\"
  \"--a a,b --b child\"
  \"--a a,b --b hero\"
  \"--a a,b --b mouse\"
  \"--a a,b --b knife\"
  \"--a a,b --b analysis\"
  \"--a a,b --b psychosis\"
  \"--a a,b --b fireman\"
  \"--a a,b --b 'wish maker'\"
)
for args in \""'${cases[@]}"; do
  py_out=$(eval "/workspace/dataset/test12_executable $args")
  js_out=$(eval "node /output/test12.mjs $args")
  if [ "$py_out" != "$js_out" ]; then
    printf '"'Mismatch for %s\\nPY:\\n%s\\nJS:\\n%s\\n' \""'$args" "$py_out" "$js_out"
    exit 1
  fi
done
printf '"'all_cli_output_cases_matched\\n'

error_cases=(
  \"\"
  \"--a x\"
  \"--b item\"
  \"--c z\"
  \"--a x --b item --c z\"
  \"foo --a x\"
  \"--a --b item\"
  \"--a x --b\"
  \"--help\"
  \"-h\"
  \"--h\"
  \"--he\"
  \"-hx\"
  \"--help=1\"
)
for args in \""'${error_cases[@]}"; do
  set +e
  py_out=$(eval "/workspace/dataset/test12_executable $args" 2>&1)
  py_status=$?
  js_out=$(eval "node /output/test12.mjs $args" 2>&1)
  js_status=$?
  set -e
  expected=$(printf '"'%s' \""'$py_out" | sed '"'s/test12_executable/test12.mjs/g')
  if [ \""'$expected" != "$js_out" ] || [ "$py_status" != "$js_status" ]; then
    printf '"'Mismatch for error case %s\\nPY status:%s\\nJS status:%s\\nExpected:\\n%s\\nActual:\\n%s\\n' \""'$args" "$py_status" "$js_status" "$expected" "$js_out"
    exit 1
  fi
done
printf '"'all_parser_cases_matched\\n'"
